If smoking cessation is an option and the patient smokes, it wins — unless the question is scoped to a specific organ ("risk of nephropathy progression" → ACE-I/BP; "microvascular complications" → A1c). Lifestyle answers are traps when vague ("recommend exercise") and winners when specific and high-magnitude (smoking or alcohol cessation).

edits.find: Petechiae with a count of 8,000 in a healthy young woman → ITP → steroids/IVIG, not transfusion (transfused platelets get consumed too) · heparin day 5–10 with a 50% drop → HIT → stop heparin, start argatroban, never transfuse · clumps on the smear → pseudothrombocytopenia from EDTA → repeat in a citrate tube — the one time "recheck the count" is correct · DDAVP is for qualitative defects (von Willebrand disease, mild hemophilia A, uremic platelet dysfunction), not for a low count.
edits.with: Petechiae with a count of 8,000 in a healthy young woman → ITP (immune thrombocytopenia). Treat with steroids or IVIG (intravenous immunoglobulin), not transfusion, because transfused platelets get consumed too · heparin day 5–10 with a 50% drop → HIT (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia). Stop heparin, start argatroban and never transfuse · clumps on the smear → pseudothrombocytopenia from EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid). Repeat the count in a citrate tube; this is the one time "recheck the count" is correct · DDAVP (desmopressin) is for qualitative defects (von Willebrand disease, mild hemophilia A, uremic platelet dysfunction), not for a low count.

edits.find: The stem's deciding words are "unprocessed" and "no supplements." A well-planned vegan diet meets most needs — the exam's fork is which nutrients cannot come from unfortified plants: B12 always, vitamin D (skin synthesis covers only ~half the requirement, less in northern latitudes), and calcium (plant sources are oxalate-bound). Iron and zinc join the list for children and menstruating women. The planted wrong answers are folate and protein — abundant in legumes, greens, and grains.
edits.with: The diet is "unprocessed", and the patient takes "no supplements." A well-planned vegan diet meets most needs. Three nutrients cannot come from unfortified plants: B12 always, vitamin D and calcium. Skin synthesis covers only ~half the vitamin D requirement, and less in northern latitudes. Plant sources of calcium are oxalate-bound. Iron and zinc join the list for children and menstruating women. Legumes, greens, and grains supply abundant folate and protein, so neither needs supplementing.
